maria: Quick heads-up — we see a p99 jump on dedicated-pool-3 starting ~18:23 UTC. Baseline p95 fine, p99 ~2.1x normal. Dashboard: https://console/redwood/observability/cluster/dedicated-pool-3 :eyes:
ajay: saw that. any pattern with sequence length or tool calls?
ralph: initial grep — top sessions are long prompts (>8k tokens) and a handful of tool-calling traces with repeated tool callbacks. also KV cache hit drops in the same window.
maria: copying profiler snippet: ```
# perf top-like summary
hot kernels: attention_fused_seq, gelu_fast, kv_load
avg seq len bucket: 1-512: 78%, 513-2048: 16%, >2048: 6%
p99 lat contributors: kv_load(34%), matmul(28%), host-sync(20%)
```
leila: interesting that kv_load is so high. could be repeated KV cache misses due to tool-generated prefixes and dynamic req ids. any churn in KV keys?
ralph: yes — we correlated request metadata: calls that do tool-calling create ephemeral context ids and append tool outputs, causing poor prefix reuse. KV keys are different, so prefix/KV cache yields drop from 90%->42% in those sessions.
ajay: so tail is a combo: long sequence compute + KV thrash + kernel choice being suboptimal for long+short mix. kernel chooser picks `attention_fused_seq` (fast for <1k) but we end up with >2k occasionally, so we pay kernel-switch penalty + poor batching.\maria: timeline: kernel switch overheads coincide with microbatch boundary & kernel recompile logs. deploy-bot: deploy 19876 rolled out to runtime canaries at 18:05 UTC.
perf-bot: Detect: spike-correlated-change set=kernel-chooser-weighted at 18:04 UTC. Rule match: kernel-chooser:enable_alpha=true.
leila: that config flip probably biased chooser towards lower-latency kernels for majority short sequences. didn’t account for the heavy long-prompt tail.
ralph: reproducer notes: run a mixed generator load with 95% short (<=512) and 5% long (>=2048) with ~10% tool-calls appended. observed p99 increases by 60% compared to all-short baseline. KV hit drops and we see repeated small microbatches trying to maintain SLO and ending up with more host-sync.
ajay: hypothesis: microbatch sizing + hedging interacts badly. When a long request arrives it stalls a microbatch, freeing other slots -> runtime picks suboptimal kernel and sometimes triggers kv eviction policy because tool outputs alter keyspace.
maria: suggested mitigations: 1) add seq-length aware kernel-chosen threshold (if 5% of batch > L => pick long-kernel) 2) cap token budget per request to avoid runaway tool loops 3) isolate tool-calls into a separate queue with higher batching patience 4) increase KV per-tenant working set or shard keys by stable prefix.
leila: quick patch idea: kernel-chooser should use a 2-pass: sample first tokens in batch to estimate distribution then pick kernel and pre-warm kv for top-k prefixes. cheap but reduces kernel flip.
ralph: also add a tiny KV bloom for ephemeral tool keys so we avoid treating tool output as unique every time (coalesce similar tool outputs).
ajay: can we A/B gate changes? prefer A: disable the new kernel-chooser weight in canaries -> see if p99 drops. B: add isolation queue for tool-calls on a small pool and monitor p99.
maria: rolling back alpha flag now in canaries. leila, can you prototype the 2-pass sampler? small perf test harness would be enough.
leila: on it. I'll push a branch with sampler + sample config: ```json
{"sampler_window": 8, "long_thresh": 1024, "decision_policy": "majority_or_max"}
```
perf-bot: test-run queued: mixed_long_short_tool_2026-03-18-19: queued.
ralph: we should also add logging to kv eviction reporter to capture ephemeral key ratios for postmortem. small change.
maria: agreed. action items: rollback alpha flag (ajay done), add sampler patch PR (leila), kv eviction logging PR (ralph), run targeted load test and report p95/p99 + kv hit. Aim to close loop by EOD. :thumbsup:
ajay: i'll validate rollback metrics once canary stabilizes.
leila: starting dev run now, will post sample results when ready.
perf-bot: mixed_long_short_tool_2026-03-18-19: finished. summary: p99 down 18% on canary after rollback; kv-hit restored from 46%->87% for affected sessions. Full logs: https://perf/reports/1987659999
maria: great, looks like kernel-chooser change was the dominant factor + KV thrash amplified. we'll keep the sampler idea but treat kernel-weights as conservative by default. thanks team.
ajay: follow-up: proposal doc for longer term — sequence-aware batching + tool-call isolation queue + KV bloom. I'll draft and drop in #eng-runtime later.
ralph: noted for postmortem. closing thread once PRs merged. :white_check_mark:
